prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map shows an outdoor ground scene from a steep downward egocentric viewpoint where the camera wearer's lower legs, forearms, and hands in the lower foreground are brightest (0.2–0.8 m away), while the flat dirt ground below is darker (~1.0–1.5 m away). On the ground in frames 1–4, a translucent plastic bag of colourful balls on the far left and a cluster of loose yellow and orange balls in the upper-left are ~1.0–1.3 m from the camera wearer and ~0.2–0.3 m apart, while a long blade on the right is held within the wearer's right-arm reach (~0.7–1.0 m) as a second person's hand enters at the top-right in frame 4 (~1.1 m away). In frame 5, the camera tilts and shifts rightward to reveal two other people within ~0.5–1.2 m (roughly 0.3–0.5 m apart from each other): a person in red and brown trousers standing/crouching on the left with their right hand extended forward within 0.4 m of the lens—partially occluding the wearer's raised left hand (0.2–0.3 m away) and the ground—and a second person in purple squatting on the right (~0.9–1.2 m away) reaching into a dark bag of balls while both bodies remain cropped above the chest so their faces and gaze directions are out of view. Across frames 1–4 the wearer's right hand advances slightly forward along the blade before the sharp camera turn and upward hand movement in frame 5 bring the wearer's left hand and the standing person's outstretched right arm much closer to the viewpoint. The depth map makes the 3D elevation of the bag of balls, the vertical drop from the wearer's knees to the ground, and the depth layering of the overlapping arms in frame 5 much clearer than in RGB alone, though it is unreliable around the dark ash and blade on the right of frames 1–4 (which sink into an overly dark hole) and flattens the raised plastic bag on the left into a smooth blob.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates parts of the people and a few small spherical objects against an unlabelled black background corresponding to the dirt ground, bags, and blade. In frames 1–4, it segments the camera wearer's crouched legs, arms, and hands at the bottom of the frame (0.3–1.0 m from the lens, with the left hand resting on the left foot and the right hand holding the ground blade within arm's reach), a blue sandal entering at the bottom-left edge in frames 3–4 (~1.1 m away), and a second person's hand at the top-right edge in frame 4 (~1.1 m away). In frame 5, as the view turns rightward, a single pink mask merges the camera wearer's raised left hand in the bottom-left foreground (~0.2–0.3 m away) with the torso and extended right arm of the person in red/brown standing to the left (~0.4–1.0 m away, oriented toward the camera/ground with their head cropped out of view), while a separate brown mask captures the squatting person in purple on the right (~0.9–1.2 m away, ~0.3–0.5 m right of the standing person, facing down toward the bag of balls within their arm's reach). The segmentation map highlights the incoming foot at the bottom-left of frame 4 and the top-right hand in frame 4 that blend into the busy ground in RGB, but it is highly unreliable across the sequence. Specifically, it splits the camera wearer's own body into multiple overlapping 'person' instances with hard rectangular mask cutoffs in frame 1, merges the wearer's hand with the adjacent standing person in frame 5, misses most of the balls, bags, and the blade entirely, and misclassifies a few orange plastic balls on the ground (~1.2 m away) as 'orange'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only 2D magenta hand skeletons on a black background and fails to detect any yellow body skeletons across all 5 frames because the people are seen from a steep top-down angle with their heads and upper torsos mostly cropped out of the frame. In frames 1, 3, and 4, a single small hand skeleton localizes the camera wearer's left hand resting on their left sandal in the bottom-left foreground (~0.7–0.9 m below the camera, ~0.3 m left of the wearer's right leg), showing the fingers oriented toward the right-front while remaining stationary within the wearer's immediate reach. In frame 2, no skeletons are detected at all, and across frames 1–4 the map completely misses the wearer's right hand gripping the blade on the right (~0.7–1.0 m away) as well as the other person's hand entering at the top-right in frame 4 (~1.1 m away). In frame 5, as the camera turns toward the two nearby people (~0.5–1.2 m away), the pose map detects only the outstretched right hand of the person in red in the upper-right foreground (~0.4–0.5 m in front of the lens, above the squatting person's hands), showing their palm and curled fingers facing toward the camera wearer. While this skeleton clarifies the exact finger articulation of the wearer's resting left hand in frames 1, 3, and 4 and the approaching hand in frame 5 against dark henna markings and cluttered backgrounds, the map is largely unreliable because it misses the wearer's raised left hand in the bottom-left of frame 5, both hands of the squatting person in purple reaching into the bag (~1.0 m away), and all full-body poses and facing directions.
